title: UI Fetch Performance Foundation
goal: Stop unnecessary broad data refreshes from making the operator console slower and harder to reason about as findings grow.
scope: Inspect the current engagement/run refresh path and implement a selected-run scoped refresh strategy for findings and related analysis data. Prefer additive client-side refresh discipline before API contract changes.
generation_reason: Product recommendation coverage audit found broad finding refetch performance was not represented as its own queued package.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Keep this slice to evidence-backed UI fetch discipline. Do not rewrite the frontend architecture or change backend contracts unless inspection proves a narrow additive endpoint is required.
notes: Measure or document the current refresh path before changing it.
Selected-run truth must remain correct after refresh optimization.

success_criteria: Engagement refresh no longer blindly reloads all run findings when selected-run scoped data is sufficient.
Selected run, findings, evidence, and report context remain consistent after refresh.
Browser or unit coverage proves stale and updated data paths.
Docs note the remaining frontend state ceiling if it still exists.
No broad framework migration is introduced.
must_not_touch: pack registry, validation, approval, deployment, or runtime binding flows

acceptance_criteria: Refresh behavior is scoped and correct for the selected run.
No stale finding state is introduced.
No frontend rewrite is bundled into the optimization.

before_promotion: The prior active task is completed and logged.
The current refetch path is inspected and documented in the work log.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with UI fetch changes and validation evidence.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with the fetch-performance baseline and remaining state-management limits.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md, or set an explicit holding state if the queue is exhausted.
